name: Itchan Kala (Inner Walled City)
tagline: The intact walled Silk Road core
description: The UNESCO-listed inner town enclosed by mud-brick walls, a compact maze of madrasas, minarets, mosques and mausoleums. You can sleep, eat and stroll among centuries-old monuments, including the turquoise Kalta Minor and the Kunya Ark fortress.
bestFor: History lovers wanting to stay among monuments and walkable heritage streets
pros: Safe and quiet in the evenings

name: Dichan Kala (Outer Town)
tagline: Everyday life beyond the inner walls
description: The outer town within Khiva's outer defensive walls, where ordinary local life carries on. It is less polished than the inner city, with family homes, small shops and cheaper guesthouses, offering a more authentic and affordable feel just outside the monuments.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads wanting authentic local life near the old town
pros: Quick walk to the inner city

name: Main Gates and Bazaar Area
description: The lively zone around Khiva's main western gates and the market, where the bazaar spills out with produce, bread and household goods. It is the town's practical hub for shopping, cheap eats and catching shared taxis to Urgench and beyond.
bestFor: Those wanting markets, cheap food and easy onward transport links
pros: Cheap bazaar produce and street food

name: Urgench
description: The regional capital about 30km from Khiva, home to the nearest airport and main railway links across Uzbekistan. Larger and more modern, it offers more shops, faster connectivity and services, making it a practical base or gateway for onward travel.
bestFor: Nomads needing an airport, faster internet or bigger-city services nearby
